speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, along with paresthesias and muscle weakness. To help narrow down the cause, have you noticed if these symptoms worsen when you turn your head or look up?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of diabetes and hypertension, which can cause nerve damage, does the weakness in your hands affect your grip strength or fine motor skills, such as buttoning a shirt or holding a cup? Additionally, have you noticed any numbness in your legs or changes in your bladder or bowel control?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

The presence of burning pain with fasciculations, absent reflexes, and progressive weakness in a 58-year-old male is highly suggestive of a motor neuron disease. While the pain and paresthesias can mimic cervical radiculopathy or diabetic neuropathy, the combination of upper and lower motor neuron signs (fasciculations and absent reflexes) points elsewhere. Could you confirm if these symptoms are strictly affecting the hands and arms, or if you have noticed similar changes in your legs, face, or tongue?
